title: Calibrating SQS Visibility Timeouts & Heartbeats
prompt: An invoice-OCR and billing-settlement service reads jobs from an SQS Standard queue (`invoice-jobs`) configured with the default `VisibilityTimeout = 30s`. Normal jobs finish in 8–12 seconds, but multi-page PDFs take 48s at p95 and up to 110s at p99. Under peak load (400 jobs/sec), 14% of jobs are picked up by a second worker at t=30s while Worker A is still running OCR and calling the payment gateway. This causes duplicate gateway charges, redundant GPU OCR runs, and `ReceiptHandleIsInvalid` / stale-delete errors when Worker A finishes at t=75s. Design the visibility-timeout lifecycle, heartbeat extension mechanism, and idempotency layer to eliminate duplicate side effects without delaying crash recovery for dead workers.

spark.summary: When an SQS Standard queue's `VisibilityTimeout` (30s) is shorter than p99 job duration (110s), SQS re-exposes in-flight messages to a second worker while the first worker is still running, causing 14% duplicate processing and wasted compute.
spark.keyTakeaway: When an SQS Standard queue's `VisibilityTimeout` (30s) is shorter than p99 job duration (110s), SQS re-exposes in-f, because SQS guarantees at-least-once delivery, pair a calibrated visibility heartbeat (`ChangeMessageVisibility` every `T/2`) with a strict idempotent consumer store so neither long jobs nor worker crashes cause duplicate side effects.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts 110s p99 Job vs. 30s Default VisibilityTimeout (SQS Standard -> Worker 1 (Spot) -> Worker 2 (Spot) -> Payment Gateway); Worker Lease Heartbeat & Settlement State Machine (PROCESSING -> SETTLED -> CRASH / MAX 900s).
